changelog:
**The configuration page was drawing itself into a third of the window.** The band of empty space below the page has been fixed twice before and came back both times; this is what it actually was. The page measures how much room it has by collapsing itself and seeing what is left of the document - but the dashboard holds a plugin page at the full height of the window whatever the page inside it does, so collapsing changed nothing, the sum came out as zero every time, and the page fell back to its minimum of 460 pixels. In a 1190-pixel window that is a third of the screen with the rest left dark. It is measured differently now, by offering the page the whole window and seeing how much too tall that turns out to be, which needs no belief about the dashboard at all. The dashboard's own padding below the page is taken as well, bar a small gap, and the shelf uses the room that frees up rather than staying at a fixed height.

**Opening a channel now shows what is on air.** The schedule was supposed to open scrolled to the now line and did not: it scrolled once, the first time the grid had a size, and at that moment the grid has no rows in it yet - so it set a scroll position that snapped straight back to the top and never tried again. A day would open at midnight with the now line an entire screen below the fold. It waits for the grid to have something to scroll now, and scrolls again on arriving anywhere new: another channel, another view, another week of a longer cycle. Between those it leaves the scrollbar alone.

**And the zoom fits what is playing.** A channel opens at the zoom that shows the programme on air properly, rather than at a fixed number - which cannot suit both a film channel with four bars in a day and a channel of forty. **Follow what's on**, beside the zoom slider, keeps it that way as the evening moves on: each time the programme changes it re-fits and re-centres. It is ticked to begin with and can be turned off per channel, and moving the slider by hand turns it off, because the zoom cannot be both worked out and set at once.

**The zoom is remembered per channel** from now on, and per view, instead of one number shared by everything. The channels are not alike and a zoom that reads one of them is useless on the next.

The rest: the clock on the now line sat exactly where a programme's name is drawn, so it was printed across whatever was airing - it is at the other end of the line now. And the Day view was captioned with the whole schedule's total, "386 scheduled" underneath a single Friday; it counts the day it is showing, and says which day and between what times.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.
